What is your favorite Kubrick film (or films) and why?

My personal favorite is Dr. Strangelove. Maybe it's because I'm a fan of absurdist wartime humor like Catch-22...but it just combines the surreal with a rushed, unrealistic and bitingly sarcastic world view.
A Clockwork Orange. It is possibly the ONLY film of its' genre. And it really does delve into some human condition.

The Killing for being a great heist caper, the outstanding performances of Sterling Hayden and Elisha Cook, and the cosmic justice at film's end. Classic film noir.

Paths of Glory for the beautiful black and white cinematography, poignant storyline, and powerful performances of Ralph Meeker, and Timothy Carey, in particular. It is a damn perfect film, one I never tire of watching.

Lolita, for the time period, beautiful cinematography, and wonderful Jazz score by Nelson Riddle. Shelley Winters was perfect as Charlotte Haze, "that brainless bah-bah," and Peter Sellers was phenomenal in a variety of parts. No one can dance as suavely as Clare Quilty. For her first film role, Sue Lyon was remarkably self-assured.

Dr. Strangelove primarily for the unforgettable scene where Slim Pickens as Major Kong, rides the bomb like a bucking bronco on his way to nuclear Armageddon. One of the most powerful scenes in film history, up there with Malcolm McDowell as Alex strapped to a chair with the electrode cap and his eyes wide open as he undergoes the Ludovico method in A Clockwork Orange. Sterling Hayden was perfect as the deranged General Jack D. Ripper who thinks fluoride in the drinking water was a communist conspiracy and is obsessed with fluids. Peter Sellers turns in not one but three tour de force performances. My favorite character though was George C. Scott as General Buck Turgidson, slapping his belly, chewing gum, and wrestling with the Russian ambassador. "Gentlemen, you can't fight in here! This is the war room!". Scott's performance makes me laugh every time I see it. Just perfect.

2001: A Space Odyssey. Because it is trippy, beautifully photographed, breathtaking, philosophical, and frightening. HAL is one of cinemas most underrated villains. My favorite scene comes in the transition when the bone is thrown into the air and comes down as the space station. That image is pure, unadulterated genius.

A Clockwork Orange. Everything about it is perfect. I never tire of watching this film.

If kubrick had lived only ten more years we might have seen him make AI and Napoleon, which I am certain would have been masterpieces.
